traceability.evidence:
Implementation and tests clearly target docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md:
1) Maintenance tools implementation - src/maintenance/index.ts - Exports all maintenance utilities with explicit traceability: - detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport - JSDoc: - @story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md - @req REQ-MAINT-DETECT / REQ-MAINT-UPDATE / REQ-MAINT-BATCH / REQ-MAINT-VERIFY / REQ-MAINT-REPORT / REQ-MAINT-SAFE
- src/maintenance/detect.ts - Function detectStaleAnnotations(codebasePath: string): string[] - Scans all files under a workspace root for @story annotations using getAllFiles(workspaceRoot). - Treats codebasePath as workspace root (resolved from process.cwd()). - Returns [] if root does not exist or is not a directory (graceful handling of missing roots). - For each file, processFileForStaleAnnotations reads content safely (try/catch on read errors) and regex-scans for @story. - handleStoryMatch(storyPath, workspaceRoot, cwd, stale) uses: - isUnsafeStoryPath + enforceProjectBoundary to avoid traversal / unsafe paths and keep checks within workspace. - Only marks a story as stale if in-project candidates exist conceptually but none exist on disk. - Multiple traceability annotations referencing REQ-MAINT-DETECT.
- src/maintenance/update.ts - updateAnnotationReferences(codebasePath: string, oldPath: string, newPath: string): number - Early-return 0 if codebasePath does not exist or is not a directory (graceful failure for invalid roots). - Escapes oldPath into a regex `(@story\s*)${escapedOldPath}` so only @story references are updated. - Iterates all files from getAllFiles(codebasePath) and calls processFileForAnnotationUpdates for each. - processFileForAnnotationUpdates(fullPath, regex, newPath, replacementCountRef) - Skips non-files (stat.isFile check) so directories/etc. are not touched. - Reads file content, uses String.replace with a callback to increment count and rewrite the story path while preserving prefix and other formatting. - Writes back only when content actually changed. - All functions marked with @story 009.0 and @req REQ-MAINT-UPDATE.
- src/maintenance/batch.ts - batchUpdateAnnotations(codebasePath, mappings) - Loops over mappings {oldPath, newPath}[] and accumulates total updates via updateAnnotationReferences. - Implements requirement REQ-MAINT-BATCH for batch updates across multiple mappings. - verifyAnnotations(codebasePath) - Calls detectStaleAnnotations and returns true when no stale annotations exist; implements REQ-MAINT-VERIFY.
- src/maintenance/report.ts - generateMaintenanceReport(codebasePath): string - Uses detectStaleAnnotations to derive stale annotations. - Returns "" if none (no-op, indicates no actions required) or a newline-joined list otherwise. - Annotated with REQ-MAINT-REPORT & REQ-MAINT-SAFE; behavior ensures report generation is safe and reversible (no mutations).
- src/maintenance/utils.ts - getAllFiles(dir: string): string[] and traverseDirectory(...) - Safe, recursive file discovery utility used by detect & update. - Validates that the input path exists and is a directory; otherwise returns an empty list (no errors thrown). - Traverses directories and collects only regular files; skips non-file entries. - Annotated with additional maintenance utility requirements (REQ-MAINT-UTILS-*, strengthening safety and robustness for maintenance operations).
- src/maintenance/cli.ts - Implements the `traceability-maint` CLI and maps requirements to user-facing behavior: - parseCliInput(rawArgv): centralizes extraction of subcommand and arguments. @req REQ-MAINT-SAFE. - runMaintenanceCli(rawArgv): main entry point; supports commands `detect`, `verify`, `report`, `update`. - For unknown commands prints error + help and returns EXIT_USAGE (2). - Wraps command handling in try/catch; unexpected errors produce a concise stderr diagnostic and EXIT_USAGE (2), satisfying REQ-MAINT-SAFE error handling. - Flag parsing (createDefaultFlags, applyFlag, parseFlags): - Supports --root, --json, --format text|json, --from, --to, --dry-run with strict validation and clear error on unsupported format values. - handleDetect(args): - Uses detectStaleAnnotations(root) and either: - Prints JSON { root, stale } when --json is used, or - Prints friendly text output including a summary and guidance to run `report` when stale annotations found. - Returns EXIT_OK (0) when no stale annotations, EXIT_STALE (1) when stale found. - Implements REQ-MAINT-DETECT + REQ-MAINT-REPORT + REQ-MAINT-SAFE. - handleVerify(args): - Uses verifyAnnotations(root) and prints a concise success or failure message. - Returns EXIT_OK (0) when annotations valid, EXIT_STALE (1) otherwise. - Implements REQ-MAINT-VERIFY + REQ-MAINT-SAFE. - handleReport(args): - Uses generateMaintenanceReport(root) and prints either: - A Markdown-style text report with a header and list of stale references, or - JSON { root, report } when format=json. - Always returns EXIT_OK (0). Implements REQ-MAINT-REPORT + REQ-MAINT-SAFE. - handleUpdate(args): - Requires --from and --to; otherwise prints an error plus help and returns EXIT_USAGE (2). - Supports --dry-run: - Uses generateMaintenanceReport(root) to estimate affected stale count. - Prints a clear, human-readable summary of what would be changed, without touching files, or prints structured JSON when --json is also passed. - Without --dry-run, calls updateAnnotationReferences(root, from, to) and prints the number of updated annotations (with pluralization) or JSON { root, from, to, updated }. - Returns EXIT_OK (0) on success. - Implements REQ-MAINT-UPDATE, REQ-MAINT-BATCH (via underlying batch/update tools), and REQ-MAINT-SAFE (dry-run and explicit parameter validation). - printHelp(): prints detailed usage text for all subcommands and options, providing discoverable UX per REQ-MAINT-SAFE. - Module-level execution guard calls process.exit(runMaintenanceCli(process.argv)) when run as a script.
2) Packaging & integration - package.json - "bin": { "traceability-maint": "lib/src/maintenance/cli.js" } - Confirms CLI is packaged and exposed under the required name. - "files": ["lib", "README.md", "LICENSE"] ensures lib/ (including compiled CLI) is published. - Maintenance tools are part of the main plugin package and integrate with the existing project and ESLint-related tooling.
3) Tests mapped to the story & requirements Maintenance tests are explicitly traceable to this story and requirements via @story/@req annotations:
- tests/maintenance/cli.test.ts - Header: - @story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md - @req REQ-MAINT-DETECT / REQ-MAINT-VERIFY / REQ-MAINT-REPORT / REQ-MAINT-UPDATE / REQ-MAINT-SAFE - Tests: - "[REQ-MAINT-DETECT] detect exits with code 0 and message when no stale annotations" - Asserts exit code 0 and console log "No stale @story annotations found." when runMaintenanceCli(..., "detect"). - "[REQ-MAINT-VERIFY] verify exits with code 0 when annotations valid" - Creates a valid story + annotation and asserts exit code 0 and exactly one log message. - "[REQ-MAINT-REPORT] report prints human-readable summary and exits 0" - Asserts exit code 0, report content includes a human-readable header and stale story path. - "[REQ-MAINT-UPDATE] update performs replacements and exits 0" - Verifies CLI updates @story old.path.md -> new.path.md in a real file and exits with 0. - "[REQ-MAINT-SAFE] update requires --from and --to and exits 2 when missing" - Verifies missing required flags cause exit code 2 and both error and help output. - "[REQ-MAINT-SAFE] dry-run does not modify files and exits 0" - Ensures --dry-run leaves files unchanged and returns 0. - "[REQ-MAINT-DETECT] detect supports --json output" - Verifies JSON output structure and that stale list includes the stale story name; exit code 1 when stale found.
- tests/maintenance/detect.test.ts - @story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS, @req REQ-MAINT-DETECT. - Tests: - No stale annotations -> returns []. - Single stale annotation (missing story file) -> array of length 1 containing the stale story.
- tests/maintenance/detect-isolated.test.ts - @story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS, @req REQ-MAINT-DETECT. - Tests additional behaviors and edge cases: - Non-existent directory -> returns []. - Nested directories with multiple stale annotations detected correctly. - Permission-denied directory causes detectStaleAnnotations to throw (low-level behavior), which is then handled by the CLI try/catch for user-facing safety. - Security validation test ensures unsafe/invalid @story paths (traversal, absolute outside paths, invalid extension) are not stat'ed, while legitimate in-workspace .story.md paths are checked.
- tests/maintenance/update-isolated.test.ts - @story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS, @req REQ-MAINT-UPDATE. - Tests: - Actually updates @story old.path.md to new.path.md and returns count 1. - Returns 0 when target directory does not exist.
- tests/maintenance/update.test.ts - @story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS, @req REQ-MAINT-UPDATE. - Tests that updateAnnotationReferences returns 0 when no updates are made.
- tests/maintenance/report.test.ts - @story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS, @req REQ-MAINT-REPORT and REQ-MAINT-SAFE. - Tests: - Returns empty string when no operations / no stale annotations. - Returns a string containing the stale story name when a stale annotation exists.
- tests/maintenance/batch.test.ts - @story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS, @req REQ-MAINT-BATCH and REQ-MAINT-VERIFY. - Tests: - batchUpdateAnnotations(tmpDir, []) returns 0 (handles empty mapping set safely). - verifyAnnotations(tmpDir) returns true when annotations are valid (story file exists).
- tests/maintenance/index.test.ts - @story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS, @req REQ-MAINT-SAFE. - Verifies that all maintenance utilities are exported from src/maintenance/index.ts and are functions: - detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, generateMaintenanceReport.
4) Documentation - README.md (Maintenance CLI section, lines ~96–140) - Introduces the `traceability-maint` CLI and explains its purpose: maintain and audit @story annotations repository-wide. - Documents commands: - detect – scan workspace for @story annotations referencing missing stories. - verify – verify that no stale @story annotations exist. - report – generate human-readable or JSON report of stale references. - update – apply safe, scripted updates when story files are renamed. - Provides concrete usage examples, including JSON report and update for renamed story paths. - Points to API Reference section (user-docs/api-reference.md#maintenance-api-and-cli) for deeper detail.
- docs/decisions/adr-maintenance-cli-interface.md - Explicitly references Story 009.0 and describes the chosen CLI design: - Binary name `traceability-maint`, implemented in src/maintenance/cli.ts and compiled to lib/src/maintenance/cli.js. - Command semantics (detect, verify, report, update), exit codes, and error-handling approach. - Safety features like dry-run for update and clear exit codes. - Confirms alignment with story intent and acceptance criteria and documents future incremental improvements.
5) Test run - Command executed via tooling: - npm test -- --ci --no-watchAll --verbose - Output: - > eslint-plugin-traceability@1.0.5 test - > jest --ci --bail --ci --no-watchAll --verbose - The command completed successfully (no errors reported by the tool), indicating that all Jest tests, including those for the 009.0 maintenance tools, are passing.
traceability.notes:
Story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md is clearly and comprehensively implemented.
All core requirements are covered by concrete code and passing tests: - REQ-MAINT-DETECT: detectStaleAnnotations implements detection of stale @story references, with tests for empty, simple, nested, security-related, and invalid-directory scenarios. The CLI exposes this via the `detect` command with both text and JSON output and appropriate exit codes. - REQ-MAINT-UPDATE: updateAnnotationReferences safely rewrites @story paths across a codebase, only touching matching annotations and only writing when changes occur. Isolated and CLI tests confirm correct behavior (including directory-not-exist behavior). - REQ-MAINT-BATCH: batchUpdateAnnotations provides batch updates across multiple mappings, and is tested (at least for the empty-mappings case) plus used as the basis for bulk operations in the maintenance module. - REQ-MAINT-VERIFY: verifyAnnotations uses the detection logic to confirm health of annotations and is tested both programmatically and via the CLI `verify` command. - REQ-MAINT-REPORT: generateMaintenanceReport produces a simple but functional report of stale annotations, and the CLI `report` command presents this in text or JSON form; tests assert both report content and exit code behavior. - REQ-MAINT-SAFE: Safety is addressed through argument validation, dry-run mode for updates, early returns for invalid roots, secure path handling in detection (avoiding traversal and unsafe paths), and a CLI-wide error trap that converts internal errors into clear messages and non-zero exit codes.
Acceptance criteria are met: - Core Functionality: Detection and update tools exist as both programmatic APIs and a dedicated CLI, and are demonstrably working via tests. - Quality Standards: Operations are conservative (no auto-formatting or structural rewrites), only touch @story references when needed, and dry-run support allows users to preview effects, helping preserve code functionality and formatting. - Integration: Tools live in src/maintenance/, are exported by src/maintenance/index.ts, shipped via the package bin field, and leverage the same story-reference utilities as the existing ESLint rules, aligning with the existing project structure and validation logic. - User Experience: The CLI has clear commands, help text, exit codes, and log messages, and the README documents usage with concrete examples. - Error Handling: Missing directories, invalid roots, and bad arguments are handled without crashing; permission errors at the low level are caught and surfaced through the CLI’s error handling; unsafe paths are filtered out by security checks. - Documentation: The Maintenance CLI is documented in README.md with examples, and the ADR describes the CLI design and rationale. Tests include story and requirement annotations, tying behavior directly back to this story.
Given the breadth of implementation, targeted tests, working CLI wiring, and documentation, this story is fully implemented and passes its acceptance criteria.
